title: Sarah's Key
author: Tatiana de Rosnay
summary: In 1942 a young girl is rounded up with her family in Paris, but first locks her little brother in a hiding place, planning to come back. Decades later a journalist researching the roundup stumbles onto the girl's trail.
readIf: you want a quick, emotional story about a little-known episode of the Occupation of France.
skipIf: you cannot read about children suffering, since the early chapters are very distressing.

pairings.reason: Also centres on a child's view of war and persecution, and does so with a gentler, more lyrical hand.
Follows ordinary people in occupied France, with a bigger cast and more heroism.
Another novel split between two points of view during the war, with beautifully measured prose.
